# Dogleg Data

> Golf's conventional wisdom, tested against real data. Sourced analysis for the 8-to-30 handicap.

Dogleg Data is an independent golf analytics publication for the golfer who plays a $65 muni and gets advice built from tour numbers. Every claim traces to a named source: Broadie's ShotLink data, Stagner and Arccos amateur numbers, USGA and R&A rough studies, GOLFTEC fitting data. Where a figure is extrapolated rather than pulled straight from a source, the chart labels it modeled.

## Pages

- [Home](https://doglegdata.com/): Site overview and the latest analysis, "230 Yards Is Enough: How Far You Need to Drive It at Your Handicap."
- [230 Yards Is Enough](https://doglegdata.com/tee-shot-distance/): How far you need to hit it to score like your handicap: 230 yards for a 10-handicap on a 360-yard par 4, why the 3-wood saves you almost nothing, and the lost-ball rate where a backup club beats the driver. Benchmark modeled, calibrated to published Shot Scope scoring.
- [Tee shot calculator](https://doglegdata.com/tee-shot-distance/tool.html): Enter a par 4, your handicap, and your typical drive; get the strokes-gained verdict, the cost line for the hole, and the club comparison.
- [Fairway vs. Rough, by Handicap](https://doglegdata.com/fairway-vs-rough/): The fairway is worth 75 yards to a tour pro at 150 out, and 17 to a 20-handicap, with sourced data you can check yourself.
- [Tools](https://doglegdata.com/fairway-vs-rough/dashboard.html): A scramble decision calculator, break-even explorer, and Monte Carlo GIR simulator, built on the same dataset as the first post.
- [About](https://doglegdata.com/about/): Who runs Dogleg Data and the verification standard behind every analysis.
- [Cite](https://doglegdata.com/cite/): Chart pack for podcasts, video, and articles. Every chart free to use with credit, sources on the image.
